name: Reasoning about Uncertainty: Do Reasoning Models Know When They Don't Know?
authors: Zhiting Mei, Christina Zhang, Tenny Yin, Justin Lidard, Ola Shorinwa, Anirudha Majumdar (Princeton University)
reflection_type: calibration/probing | verbal-self-critique (introspective UQ: a second-stage model verbally critiques the first model's chain-of-thought to recalibrate its confidence)
feedback_source: self-generated (the reasoning model introspects on its own chain-of-thought traces via self-verbalized prompting; ground-truth labels are used only externally by the authors to compute calibration metrics ECE/MCE, not fed back to the model). Black-box only — no logit/internal-state access.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine (two-stage introspective pipeline: stage 1 answers + verbalizes confidence; stage 2 reasons over the stage-1 trace to revise the confidence estimate; limited to two stages in this work, optimal stage count left to future work)
reflection_object: reasoning chain (the model reflects on its own chain-of-thought trace and final answer to identify flaws and re-estimate confidence). It does NOT modify the output answer itself — the second stage is restricted to reasoning about uncertainty/confidence, deliberately not updating the original answer to avoid hallucination/vacillation. So the modified artifact is the confidence/uncertainty estimate over the existing answer.
requires_training: none (all models evaluated zero-shot via API without any fine-tuning; introspection is purely prompt/inference-time)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (the reasoning model itself, in a second introspective stage, judges and re-scores the confidence of its own first-stage reasoning trace; no separate trained reward/critic model is used)
distillation_target: none (no reusable artifact is distilled; introspective UQ operates per-query at inference time and produces a recalibrated confidence estimate, not stored memory/skills/weights)
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered (introspective UQ is a prompt/scaffold-engineered two-stage procedure layered on top of reasoning models; however the paper analyzes RL-emergent reasoning depth and finds that emergent deeper reasoning worsens calibration/overconfidence)
memory_type: none (no persistent memory; the only state passed forward is the stage-1 chain-of-thought trace handed to the stage-2 introspection prompt within a single query)
memory_persistence: within-episode (the first-stage reasoning trace is provided to the second-stage introspection within the same query; nothing persists across questions/tasks/sessions)
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level (introspection targets the overall correctness/confidence of the full response; the second stage identifies flaws in the chain-of-thought to adjust a single answer-level confidence score rather than localizing/correcting individual reasoning steps). The paper notes step-level/intermediate-step calibration benchmarks as future work.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (calibration and introspection are performed per question on a single task instance; no experience is transferred across tasks)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision (the second stage post-hoc revises the confidence estimate after the answer is produced; it explicitly does NOT correct the answer in-flight, so this is confidence revision rather than answer recovery)
task_domains: QA/reasoning (multiple-choice and open-ended question answering spanning arithmetic, science, humanities, professional knowledge, and factuality); analysis/UQ of reasoning models
benchmarks: ARC-Challenge, GPQA, MMLU (abstract algebra, professional accounting, professional medicine, international law, sociology subsets), StrategyQA, SimpleQA. Calibration measured via Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) with reliability diagrams.
headline_result: Reasoning models are systematically overconfident: self-verbalized confidence is often >85%, especially on incorrect responses; overconfidence grows with deeper reasoning (on consistently wrong-answered questions, o3-Mini shows a ~7% absolute ECE increase from low- to high-reasoning, Claude ~2%). Introspective UQ improves calibration for o3-Mini and DeepSeek R1 (largest gains on SimpleQA with the more conservative IUQ-Medium/IUQ-High prompts) but worsens it for Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
baselines: Self-verbalized UQ prompt strategies without introspection: zero-shot basic prompting, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, multi-step prompting, and Top-K prompting. Also contextualized against prior reported calibration of non-reasoning models (e.g., pre-RLHF GPT-4 had lower/better ECE on an MMLU subset).
gains_vs_baseline: Introspection effect is model- and dataset-dependent rather than a uniform gain. Averaged over models, IUQ-Low marginally increases ECE while IUQ-Medium and IUQ-High decrease ECE (largest reductions on the hardest dataset, SimpleQA); MCE increases across datasets. For deeper reasoning on GPQA, low->high reasoning gives +10.8% accuracy and -5.5% ECE; but on saturated/hard datasets (e.g., SimpleQA) deeper reasoning increases ECE. Claude's accuracy/calibration trade-off: Claude is the best-calibrated model and ~2% more accurate than DeepSeek and >4% more accurate than o3-Mini, with weaker accuracy-ECE correlation (r=-0.69 vs near -1.0 for others).
compute_cost_profile: Introspective UQ roughly doubles inference cost vs a single self-verbalized pass (two reasoning stages per query: one answer-generation pass plus one introspection pass over the trace). The reasoning-depth study additionally scales thinking-token budget across RE-Low/RE-Medium/RE-High levels, increasing inference time and energy with deeper reasoning. No training cost (zero-shot API evaluation).
known_limitations: Analysis is restricted to black-box self-verbalized UQ (no access to closed-source logits/internal states); introspection limited to two stages (optimal stage count left to future work); Gemini excluded from reasoning-depth and introspection analyses due to insufficient support for reasoning-token budget / reasoning-trace analysis, and Grok 3 Beta not benchmarked (no access). Many existing benchmarks are saturated, making them uninformative for UQ; the work calls for new UQ benchmarks (including intermediate-step calibration). Introspection is not uniformly beneficial — it degrades Claude 3.7 Sonnet's calibration, possibly due to closed-source implementation details. Reasoning-depth tuning hurts format/completion compliance, especially in scientific domains (GPQA).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: self-verify (the model recalibrates confidence purely by introspecting on its own chain-of-thought; no external tool/verifier, oracle label, or environment reward is given to the model. Ground-truth labels are used only by the authors offline to score calibration via ECE/MCE, not as feedback to the model.)
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent (introspective confidence recalibration is net-positive for o3-Mini and DeepSeek R1 — especially with conservative prompts on hard benchmarks like SimpleQA — but net-negative for Claude 3.7 Sonnet; IUQ-Low can even raise average ECE. This is confidence self-correction, not answer self-correction, since the answer is intentionally left unchanged.)
calibration_effect: mixed (a central, explicitly measured finding). Reasoning models are overconfident, and deeper RL-induced reasoning generally degrades calibration / worsens overconfidence — a 'reasoning tax' on calibration — particularly on incorrect responses where deeper reasoning reinforces a misguided thought process. Introspection improves calibration for some models (o3-Mini, DeepSeek R1) but worsens it for others (Claude 3.7 Sonnet).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (the paper is an analysis/UQ study of reasoning-model calibration and overconfidence, not a multi-agent failure-attribution method; introspection identifies flaws in a single model's own reasoning trace to adjust confidence but does not produce a failure-mode taxonomy or attribute responsibility across agents/steps)
failure_mode_addressed: Overconfidence / poor calibration of reasoning models (confidently wrong responses / hallucinations). Closely related to the 'reasoning tax' and overthinking-style failure modes: deeper reasoning increases confidence on incorrect answers by reinforcing a flawed thought process. Also surfaces 'superficial self-reflection' risk — introspection does not uniformly help and can entrench overconfidence (e.g., Claude).
builds_on: Self-verbalized / black-box UQ for LLMs (e.g., Tian et al.; Xiong et al.; Lin et al.; verbalized confidence and Top-K prompting); calibration foundations (ECE/MCE, proper scoring rules, Guo et al.); chain-of-thought and multi-step prompting (Wei et al.; Kojima et al.); findings that RLHF degrades token-level calibration (OpenAI GPT-4 report). Targets RL-trained reasoning models: Claude 3.7, o3-Mini, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking, DeepSeek R1.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by subsequent calibration/UQ-of-reasoning-models work, e.g., 'Process Supervision of Confidence Margin for Calibrated LLM Reasoning' (2026), 'Unsupervised Confidence Calibration for Reasoning LLMs from a Single Generation' (2026), 'How Uncertainty Estimation Scales with Sampling in Reasoning Models' (2026), 'Confidence Should Be Calibrated More Than One Turn Deep' (2026), 'Confidence Before Answering: A Paradigm Shift for Efficient LLM Uncertainty Estimation' (2026), and 'When Is Thinking Enough? Early Exit via Sufficiency Assessment for Efficient Reasoning' (2026).
citation_count: 32 (Semantic Scholar, as of 2026-06; influential citation count 3)
reasoning_model_native: Yes — the paper specifically targets o1/R1-era reasoning models with built-in RL-induced multi-step reasoning (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1, o3-Mini, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking) and analyzes how their native reasoning depth affects calibration; introspective UQ leverages the models' reasoning ability to reflect on their own chain-of-thought.
on_policy_distillation_link: Weak/indirect. No distillation is performed; the method is purely inference-time. The authors propose (as future work) training reasoning models via reinforcement learning to explicitly reason about their own uncertainty/knowledge boundaries, which is conceptually adjacent to on-policy reflection optimization but is not implemented here.
sample_efficiency: Introspective UQ uses two inference passes per query (one answer pass + one introspection pass over the trace); the reasoning-depth study sweeps three reasoning-effort levels (RE-Low/Medium/High). No iterative trial budget beyond the two stages (stage count capped at two, with optimal depth left to future work).
